title: $31 in checking, a $48 car insurance debit on Nov 23 and payday after it: her savings is her emergency fund, so Dev lays out selling $50 of a VTI position that is up $212

dev_must_notice.what: Checking is $31.00 available after the $142.00 Discount Tire charge on Nov 14. The $48.00 SafeRoute car insurance (due Sat Nov 21, it posts Mon Nov 23) would leave her $17.00 below zero, and her next paycheck comes Nov 27, after it. Moving the date costs a $10 late fee she told Dev about. Her $240.00 savings is the emergency fund she said is only for real emergencies, and the brokerage account holds $0.00 in cash. Her VTI position is worth $812.40 against $600.40 paid, up $212.00, bought Mar 14, 2025 (held over a year).

best_fix.what: One push tonight before dinner: "Checking is $31.00 and the $48.00 car insurance comes out Monday Nov 23, before your Nov 27 paycheck. Moving the date costs a $10 late fee, your savings is your emergency fund, and the brokerage has no cash. Your VTI is up $212.00 since you bought it. Selling $50 of it covers the insurance and leaves $33.00 in checking until payday. About $13 of that $50 is gain, held over a year, so it counts as long-term." Buttons: [Show me the steps] [Not now]. The steps are numbered: open the brokerage, sell $50 of VTI before Wed Nov 18 so it settles, send the $50 to Lakeside checking, which usually takes a few business days (assumption). Dev links to the brokerage and never sells or moves anything. Dev also states what it costs her: a small taxable gain, and that Dev can't say what the price will do. If she says not now, one reminder Thu Nov 19 morning that the transfer window is closing.
best_fix.why: It follows the owner's order. A bill move has a $10 fee, savings is her emergency fund and this isn't an emergency, the brokerage has no cash, so the last option is a small sale from an investment that is up. $50 covers the $48 debit with a $2 margin and keeps checking positive through Nov 27. Only facts: what it is worth, what she paid, how long she held it. No prediction, no card balance, no pay counted before it lands.

must_not: predict the market or say VTI will rise, fall or is a good time to sell
move money for her, place a sale or start the transfer: Dev lays out the steps and she does them
touch the emergency fund for a non-emergency: the $240.00 savings stays out
suggest the credit card, a cash advance or any loan to cover the $17.00
count the Nov 27 paycheck as money she already has
say selling is the right choice or give tax advice beyond the facts of how long she held it and the size of the gain
suggest selling more than the $50 shown, or the whole position
send the push during family dinner, Mon to Fri 6:30 to 7:45 PM
assumptions: Payday is every other Friday; the Nov 27 paycheck is not counted. Hourly pay is not predicted.
A VTI sale settles the next business day and a transfer to checking takes 1 to 3 more business days, so selling by Wed Nov 18 lands before the Nov 23 debit.
The brokerage holds only the VTI position and no uninvested cash. The sale amount is an even $50 for simplicity. About $13.05 of $50 is gain at her average cost.
The ACH insurance debit authorizes Sat Nov 21 and posts Mon Nov 23.
The $31.00 available includes a $6.02 App Store charge still pending (tx-2026-11-16-app-store). The tire charge was authorized Nov 14 and posted Nov 16.
Not legal or tax advice: Dev shows holding period and gain and says a tax may apply; a legal check on suggestions about selling securities is open (vision, section 15, item 14).

known.fact: SafeRoute adds a $10 late fee if the car insurance isn't paid by the 21st, so the date can't slide

tempting.suggestion: send the push during family dinner, Mon to Fri 6:30 to 7:45 PM
tempting.why_wrong: she eats dinner with her family at home most nights between 6:30 and 7:45 PM
